source.title: Structured Dropout Variational Inference for Bayesian Neural Networks
source.authors: S. Nguyen; Duong Nguyen; Khai Nguyen; K. Thân; H. Bui; Nhat Ho

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplement are present; no evident truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports held-out classification results for dropout-based methods and a direct VSD optimizer comparison, but does not test random-label memorization, interpolation, or train–test gaps.
record.gate_note: Results comparing VSD, MC Dropout, and Variational Dropout with MAP bear on dropout and held-out error. The optimizer comparison reports VSD with Adam versus SGD. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares dropout-based classifiers with deterministic MAP baselines and directly compares Adam with momentum SGD for VSD. These results bear on V6 and V4, although the dropout comparisons also change inference and prediction procedures, and the optimizer tuning protocol is incompletely specified.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that VSD offers expressive, computationally practical Bayesian inference with competitive generalization, calibration and uncertainty estimation. They advocate SGD over Adam in their additional experiments. The record broadly captures this, but ResNet18 accuracy improves slightly only on CIFAR100 and decreases slightly on CIFAR10; the clearer ResNet18 improvements are in NLL and ECE.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Bayesian variational dropout and compares its predictive metrics and optimizer choices. It does not reproduce the claim's random-label memorization, train–test-gap, or magnitude-aware sharpness procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and dataset/architecture change the VSD accuracy comparison; the study also varies the number of Householder transformations and reports predictive metrics, but those are not measurements of the claim's train–test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 9 reports final-layer spectral norms and stable ranks, not magnitude-aware sharpness or train–test gaps. Contrary to the record's blanket summary, MNIST MLP VSD has the highest spectral norm, 2.05 versus MAP 1.47, MCD 1.93 and VD 1.88.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VSD lowers final-layer stable rank in the reported comparisons and lowers spectral norm in the reported CNN comparisons, but not in the MNIST MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: VSD improves several calibration, predictive-entropy and out-of-distribution detection measures; regression experiments evaluate RMSE and predictive likelihood.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured Bayesian dropout can improve predictive uncertainty and regression performance relative to selected approximate-inference baselines.

record.problems: The comparison uses different inference procedures, so MAP is not an isolated dropout ablation. Several comparison results are inherited from prior papers. Optimizer evidence is limited to VSD with Adam versus SGD on two architectures and two datasets. The stated spectral norm and stable-rank results do not measure train–test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted further test metrics such as NLL, ECE, calibration and out-of-distribution detection, as they do not measure the test-error effects specified in V4 or V6. Table 3, Tables 4–5, Table 12, and Appendix I.6 contain these additional metrics. Table 9 reports norm and stable-rank comparisons, but not train–test gaps, so they are summarized under fits_no_version rather than entered as version rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and training to zero error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Equal or better training performance; language benchmarks; other adaptive optimizers; broader optimizer tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers during training. Equal tuning budgets and the precise SGD schedule are not established.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

Very small classification training sets, excessive dropout causing underfitting, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Bayesian prediction and method-specific regularization prevent an isolated estimate of adding dropout alone.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness, its relationship with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add dropout-versus-MAP accuracy comparisons from Table 4. For CIFAR10/CIFAR100/SVHN/STL10 respectively: MAP 69.58/40.23/87.56/65.70; MCD 75.22/42.91/88.03/63.65; VD 77.28/43.10/90.76/65.48; VSD 78.21/46.85/91.62/67.98. These include the omitted STL10 failures. The record's rows_left_out excludes additional metrics, but does not declare omission of these accuracy comparisons.

Add dropout-versus-MAP accuracy comparisons from Table 5. For CIFAR10/CIFAR100/SVHN/STL10 respectively: MAP 86.34/55.38/95.32/71.26; MCD 87.47/59.28/95.78/72.28; VD 87.68/56.80/96.11/73.29; VSD 87.44/60.15/96.41/74.50. Include the reported SDs and augmentation conditions.

record.verdict_notes: V7 is untested, rather than tested but unextracted. The retained MAP, MCD, VD and VSD classification results are the study's own experiments; inherited VMG, SLANG and ELRG comparisons should not be treated as new measurements. Reciprocal optimizer rows represent four comparisons, not eight. Smaller improvements than VSD do not by themselves qualify V6, which specifies no minimum improvement.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison of the kind specified.
Tests VSD with Adam versus SGD on AlexNet and ResNet18, on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. Does not test other adaptive optimizers, language benchmarks, broader tuning, or switching during training.

Reports test classification error for dropout-based Bayesian methods and MAP across several datasets and architectures. Does not test classic dropout settings on very small training sets or vary dropout strength to assess underfitting.
Measures spectral norms and stable ranks, but not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or training–test gaps; these measurements cannot establish the version's stated relationship.
